overview.heading: How the Image to Image Generator works
paragraphs: You add one or more reference images, write what should change, and choose Nano Banana or GPT Image, a shape, a resolution and, with GPT Image, a transparent background or an animated GIF. PiCraft sends your images and your words to the model you chose, exactly as they are, and gives you back the file the model made. There is no style menu and no crop, so the instruction you write is what steers the result.

With one image, the model starts from your photo: it can restyle it, change the light or the season, or move the subject into another setting. With several images, it can take things from each one. Refer to the images by number, in the order they appear in the form, and say what to take from each: "the dog from the first image, the sofa from the second image".

Every image is a new attempt, so the result can differ from what you pictured, and a second try is normal. Each image uses credits (1 for 1K, 2 for 2K, 3 for 4K, and 2 or 3 for an animated GIF) however many references you add, and the credits come back automatically when an image can't be made.

whatYouGet.title: The original file
whatYouGet.description: You download the image as the model returned it, at the pixel size that belongs to the shape and resolution you chose. Nothing is cropped, recolored or compressed on our side.

whatYouGet.title: A smaller JPG copy
whatYouGet.description: Next to the original comes a JPG copy that is lighter to send, post or attach.

whatYouGet.title: Several references at once
whatYouGet.description: Add up to 10 reference images with Nano Banana or up to 16 with GPT Image, and combine a subject, a place, a product and a style in one result.

whatYouGet.title: Your choice of model
whatYouGet.description: Switch between Nano Banana, GPT Image 2.6 and GPT Image 2.5 for the same photos and the same instruction, and compare the results yourself.

whatYouGet.title: A transparent background
whatYouGet.description: Choose Transparent with GPT Image to get the subject as a PNG with no background, plus a JPG copy on white.

whatYouGet.title: An animated GIF
whatYouGet.description: Choose Animated GIF with GPT Image 2.6 to turn a photo into a short looping GIF, with 6, 9 or 12 frames.

whatYouGet.title: Shapes and resolutions you choose
whatYouGet.description: Keep the framing of your photo by picking its shape, or pick a new one. Nano Banana goes from 1K to 4K and GPT Image from 1K to 2K, with the price shown next to each.

whatYouGet.title: A record of your images
whatYouGet.description: Finished images are listed under My files in the same browser for 90 days.

useCases.title: Restyle a photo
useCases.description: Turn a snapshot into a watercolor painting, a flat vector illustration or a Japanese woodblock print while keeping the composition.

useCases.title: Change the light or the season
useCases.description: Move a flat midday photo to golden hour, or a summer street to a snowy evening, and keep the rest of the scene.

useCases.title: Try a product in a new setting
useCases.description: Put a mug, a pair of sneakers or a lamp onto a marble counter or a wooden shelf, in the light you choose. Take the idea to a photographer, or use the Amazon Product Photo Maker when a marketplace needs a pure white background.

useCases.title: Combine things from several photos
useCases.description: Use two or more references to put a pet in a room, a product next to another, or a sofa from one photo into the room of another, as long as you have the right to use every photo.

useCases.title: Make a new picture from another picture
useCases.description: Upload one photo and describe the picture you want made from it: the same scene as a painting, the same product in a different setting, the same room in another season. Your photo sets the subject and the layout, and your words set the rest.

useCases.title: Redraw a sketch
useCases.description: Photograph a rough drawing, upload it and describe the finished version, such as a clean illustration or a 3D render.

useCases.title: Cut a subject out as a transparent PNG
useCases.description: Add a photo of a product, a pet or an object, say which subject to keep and choose Transparent. The PNG has no background, so it can go onto a page, a mockup or a sticker sheet.

useCases.title: Bring a photo to life as a GIF
useCases.description: Turn a picture of a pet, a mascot or a drawing into a short loop: it waves, blinks or tilts its head. Use a photo you own or have permission to use.

tips.title: Use sharp, well-lit references
tips.description: The model can only work with what it sees. A clear photo with the subject in plain view gives it more to hold on to than a dark or blurry one.

tips.title: Say what stays the same
tips.description: Phrases such as "keep the composition" and "keep everything else the same" tell the model what not to touch. Then say what to change in one sentence.

tips.title: Refer to images by number
tips.description: With several references, write "the first image" and "the second image", in the order shown in the form. Say what to take from each one.

tips.title: Say where each thing goes when you merge photos
tips.description: To combine references, name what to take from each one and where it should end up: "the lamp from the second image on the desk in the first image". A short, specific sentence gives the model less to guess.

tips.title: Pick the shape of your photo to keep its framing
tips.description: If you edit one photo and want the same framing, choose its shape, such as 4:3 or 3:2. Choose a different shape when you want the scene recomposed.

tips.title: Change one thing at a time
tips.description: If the result misses, adjust one part of the instruction and create it again. That shows you what each word does and saves credits.

tips.title: Explore small, finish large
tips.description: Try ideas at 1K, then create the final version at 2K or 4K. A larger file is a new image, not an enlargement of the first.

tips.title: For a transparent PNG, name the subject to keep
tips.description: Write "keep only the mug and remove everything else" and choose Transparent. A subject with a clear outline cuts out more cleanly than one that blends into its background; check the edge on a light and a dark background.

tips.title: For a GIF, describe the motion in order
tips.description: Say what moves and in what order: "the dog tilts its head, then wags its tail". Keep the motion simple, and keep the subject large in the photo, because the frames are drawn small.

styleGuide.heading: Nano Banana or GPT Image?
styleGuide.intro: These models all edit photos and combine references, and none of them is better at everything. These are the practical differences on PiCraft. For anything else, try your own photos on each.

items.title: Nano Banana 2.1, by Google
items.description: Takes up to 10 reference images, makes 14 shapes plus Auto, including 4:5, 5:4 and the strips 1:4, 4:1, 1:8 and 8:1, and offers 4K for every shape.

items.title: GPT Image 2.6 and 2.5, by OpenAI
items.description: Both take up to 16 reference images and make 14 shapes plus Auto, including 4:5, 5:4 and the wide 2:1 and 3:1, at 1K and 2K (Auto at 1K only). Both can leave the background transparent. Only GPT Image 2.6 makes animated GIFs.

items.title: The price
items.description: The same for every model at the same resolution, and the same however many references you add: 1 credit at 1K, 2 at 2K and 3 at 4K (GPT Image goes up to 2K). A transparent background costs the same as an image, and an animated GIF costs 2 credits for 6 frames and 3 for 9 or 12.

items.title: How long each takes
items.description: Measured on PiCraft in November 2026, at 1K: Nano Banana 2.1 took 10 to 34 seconds over 27 images, about 18 on average. GPT Image 2.5 took 13 to 56 seconds over 11 images, and 10 of them finished in under 30 seconds. In our own tests GPT Image 2.6 took about 20 to 40 seconds at 1K and 2K, with a transparent background and for GIFs. We do not have enough 4K runs to give a figure, so expect those to take longer. Times change with load. The earlier timings come from edits with reference images, which is what this page does.

items.title: When the result matters
items.description: Create the same instruction with each model and keep the better one. Results vary from image to image, so one try is not a verdict on a model.

checklist.heading: Before you download
items: Compare the result with your references: did the subject keep the details that matter, such as colors, logos and proportions?
Look closely at faces, hands and small objects, which is where AI mistakes show first.
Read every letter of any text that appears in the image.
Confirm that the shape and the pixel size shown next to the download match the place the image will go.
If you edited a photo of a place or a product that is for sale, make sure the result does not misrepresent what the buyer will get, and label it as edited where the platform requires it.
Download the files now. Generated files are deleted after 90 days.

limits: The model redraws the image, so small details can change even when you ask it not to. Check what matters, and create it again if something important is off.
A result is never exactly the same twice. For a series, keep using the earlier result as a reference.
Every model applies its own safety checks and can refuse a request. When that happens no image is made and the credits are returned.
The pixel size is set by the model. If a place needs an exact size or a pure white background, use the matching maker, which crops and exports to that spec.

Only use photos you own or have permission to use. Impersonating real people or making images that mislead people is not allowed under the [terms](/terms), and you are responsible for what you create and publish.

A GIF is a short loop drawn on one sheet, not a video. The frames are small (about 960 px square for 6 frames, 820 px for 12), the motion is simple, and the subject can change slightly from frame to frame.
A transparent background comes from GPT Image only, and GIFs from GPT Image 2.6 only. Nano Banana and GPT Image 2.5 do not make GIFs.
PiCraft makes PNG, JPG and GIF files. It does not make SVG or other vector files.
